standard_prerequisites: Context span 1226-1236: the short exact sequence 0 -> M -> direct sum over primes p of Z_(p) -> Q -> 0 where M is the kernel of the map that uses the inclusion Z_(p) -> Q on each summand
The sequence is nonsplit because there are no nonzero homomorphisms Q -> Z_(p) (a splitting would give a left inverse of the injection Q -> middle term composed to a nonzero map Q -> Z_(p))
If we localize at any prime p, the sequence becomes split (context closing sentence): the summands with q not equal to p vanish after localization at p
core_obligations: Take R = Z and the context sequence; it is nonsplit as a sequence of Z-modules (context: no nonzero homomorphisms Q -> Z_(p))
On the Zariski open D(p) the localized sequence splits (context), so the sequence is split Zariski locally
proof_roadmap: Instantiate the context sequence over Z
Nonsplitness from the vanishing of Hom(Q, Z_(p))
Splitness after localization at each prime from the context
